sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Challenge
sections.description: This section details the patient's initial symptoms, the clinical context of the emergency presentation, and the initial diagnostic dilemma between infectious, structural, and allergic causes of neck swelling.
subtopics: Presentation of progressive neck swelling and proximal muscle weakness
Initial differential diagnosis: Ludwig's angina vs. idiopathic angioedema
Role of ENT and immunology consultations in ruling out structural and histaminergic causes
Physical examination red flags: nailfold capillaroscopy and subtle cutaneous signs
Clinical reasoning for suspecting a non-histamine mediated process

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Dermatomyositis and the Anti-SAE1 Subtype
sections.description: This section provides the necessary background on dermatomyositis, specifically focusing on the anti-SAE1 antibody subtype, its associated clinical features, and the mechanism behind the rare presentation of subcutaneous edema.
subtopics: Overview of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies and dermatomyositis spectrum
Characteristics of anti-small ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme (SAE1) antibody
Pathophysiology of pseudoangioedema in dermatomyositis versus true angioedema
Association of SAE1 antibodies with dysphagia and interstitial lung disease
Immunological basis of perifascicular necrosis and microangiopathy

sections.description: This section outlines the specific investigations used to confirm the diagnosis, interpret laboratory results, and rule out malignancy or other mimics through imaging and histology.
subtopics: Interpretation of significantly elevated creatine kinase and liver transaminases
Myositis antibody panel analysis and specificity of anti-SAE1
Muscle biopsy findings: perifascicular atrophy and complement deposition (C5b-9)
Utility of MRI and PET scans in assessing muscle inflammation and malignancy screening
Evaluation of dysphagia via video fluoroscopic swallow study

sections.description: This section explains the multimodal treatment approach, justifying the choice of immunosuppressive agents, supportive care measures, and the management of treatment-related complications.
subtopics: Induction therapy with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone
Role of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in refractory or severe cases
Selection of steroid-sparing agents: Mycophenolate mofetil versus Methotrexate
Use of Rituximab in anti-SAE1 positive dermatomyositis
Management of dysphagia and airway protection including nasogastric feeding
Prophylaxis considerations for opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis jirovecii)

sections.section_title: Clinical Outcomes, Surveillance, and Key Lessons
sections.description: This section reviews the patient's recovery trajectory, the critical need for long-term malignancy surveillance, and summarizes the educational takeaways for clinicians regarding atypical dermatomyositis presentations.
subtopics: Timeline of symptom resolution and functional recovery
Malignancy risk stratification and screening guidelines (IMACS)
Long-term medication tapering and maintenance therapy planning
Importance of CK levels and skin examination in unexplained neck swelling
Clinical significance of recognizing dermatomyositis as a differential for angioedema
